column3: The Hebrew says putting their fathers with the flock’s dogs; BSB describes entrusting the fathers with the dogs.
The Hebrew describes braying rather than merely crying out.
The Hebrew leaves the singular actor unnamed and names his string; BSB explicitly names God and supplies a bow.
The Hebrew says they push away his feet and heap up their paths of disaster; BSB describes snares and siege ramps.
The Hebrew says they have no helper; BSB says no one restrains them.
The Hebrew describes his garment changing or disguising itself and girding him like a tunic collar; BSB describes grasping the garment and seizing its collar.
The Hebrew describes riding on the wind and melting him; BSB describes driving him before the wind and tossing him in a storm.
The Hebrew names a house of appointed meeting; BSB says the place appointed for all the living.
The Hebrew presents the outstretched hand and cry amid ruin; BSB explicitly describes a ruined man to whom no one extends a hand.
The Hebrew makes his inward parts the subject of boiling; BSB says he is churning within.
The Hebrew calls ostriches daughters of an ostrich; BSB says ostriches.
The Hebrew names heat without explicitly naming fever or a separate peeling action; BSB supplies fever and peeling.
